questions.key_step: Two-parameter infinite-solution condition by elimination; one familiar move.
questions.justification: Same kind of consistency analysis as 2023-P1-Q14 (L3) but with only two conditions to impose and no case analysis.

questions.key_step: Expand a parametric $3\times3$ determinant, factor out $a$, show the quadratic has no real root.
questions.justification: Routine chain with a cubic expansion, but no unfamiliar idea; same flavour as the L2 anchors for linear-system criteria.

questions.key_step: Case analysis of a parametric system (unique/none/infinite) with four statements to check.
questions.justification: Fewer parameters than 2023-P1-Q14 (L3) and each statement follows from $D$, $D_x$; routine but several checks.

questions.key_step: Determine $k$ from $D=0$, then solve a $2\times2$ system and test the options.
questions.justification: Two short routine stages, each standard; options make verification easy.

questions.key_step: Find $\alpha$ by $D=0$, $\beta$ by consistency, then build the quadratic.
questions.justification: Three short routine stages; slightly longer chain than a one-parameter question but nothing unfamiliar.

questions.key_step: Reduce to $c\,z=d$ and recognise that two conditions pin down a point; test four statements.
questions.justification: Four statements each needing a genuine check, including a line-versus-point trap - matches the anchor's matching-type consistency analysis.

questions.key_step: Root of $D$ must be tested separately; only $\lambda=-2$ is inconsistent.
questions.justification: Short chain; the trap is that $D=0$ at $\lambda=1$ is consistent. One familiar idea plus a small check.

questions.key_step: Row operations (or rank-one lemma) collapse the determinant to $2+\sin2x$; then range of sine.
questions.justification: Short determinant reduction plus an interval-range argument and squaring: a routine chain of three steps, none unfamiliar.

questions.key_step: Determinant factorisation $(\alpha-1)^2(\alpha+2)$, then check each statement at special values.
questions.justification: Four statements, each a quick check once $D$ is known; routine multi-step.

questions.key_step: Apply $\Delta=0$ and $\Delta_z=0$ to a three-equation system with two unknowns $a,b$.
questions.justification: One familiar move twice; very routine determinant expansions.

questions.key_step: Reduce to $(6-2\alpha)z=\beta-14$ and test four statements.
questions.justification: Routine consistency analysis; every statement follows from $D$ and one elimination. Level of an easy 3-equation parametric system.

questions.key_step: $D=0$ gives a quadratic in $\tan\theta$; list the roots in $[-\pi,\pi]$ and sum.
questions.justification: Three routine steps (determinant, quadratic, angle listing) with a small trap in counting solutions over $[-\pi,\pi]$.

questions.key_step: Third equation as a combination of the first two fixes $(\alpha,\beta)$; test four statements.
questions.justification: Routine system analysis, short; options make the check easy.

questions.key_step: Substituting $x=0$ collapses the determinant; then a quadratic from its roots.
questions.justification: One neat substitution and a routine finish; no unfamiliar idea.

questions.key_step: Spot the hidden row combination $10R_1+21R_2-R_3$, then two conditions.
questions.justification: Ugly numbers hide a simple relation, but the standard route (Cramer or elimination) works; two short stages.

questions.key_step: Three parametric determinants or one elimination; test four statements.
questions.justification: Same level of work as other parametric system questions; a couple of $3\times3$ expansions.

questions.key_step: Two linear determinant conditions fix $\lambda$ and $\mu$; then an algebraic value.
questions.justification: Routine: two $3\times3$ expansions and a final identity.

questions.key_step: Solve three equations, use the fourth to get $\lambda$, then a point-plane distance.
questions.justification: Three routine stages (system, parameter, distance) from two chapters; no hidden idea.

questions.key_step: Find $S$ from $D=0$ (cubic factorisation), confirm inconsistency at each root, then sum $|\lambda|$.
questions.justification: Numerical answer with a cubic determinant and a hidden consistency check at three roots; a student who skips the check still gets the key but may mis-handle a root. Moderate precision risk.

questions.key_step: Sum of determinants via linearity in the first row; triangular determinant; quadratic in $n$.
questions.justification: Numerical answer with one non-obvious idea (summing a determinant by summing a row) then routine algebra.

questions.key_step: Simplify the fractional determinant to $2\alpha^2+6\alpha+1=0$, then locate both roots in an interval.
questions.justification: Routine determinant plus quadratic root location; slightly fiddly fractions.

questions.key_step: Trap: with $\lambda=\frac12$ the constant condition is a quadratic with two roots ($\mu=1,15$), so the statement with only $\mu\neq1$ fails.
questions.justification: Parametric system with two parameters and four statements, one hidden second root; follows 2023-P1-Q14 (L3) in kind.

questions.key_step: Eliminate to $(\lambda-1)(2\lambda+1)z=13-\mu$ and notice the second exceptional value $\lambda=-\frac12$.
questions.justification: Same pattern as other parametric systems; the trap (second root) is easy to see once the factorised coefficient is written.

questions.key_step: Two determinant conditions in two parameters; the second needs a small substitution.
questions.justification: Routine; same flavour as the other infinitely-many-solutions questions.

questions.key_step: Two single-parameter determinants fix $\alpha$ and $\beta$.
questions.justification: Routine; two $3\times3$ expansions.

questions.key_step: Two linear parameter conditions from $D=0$ and $D_3=0$.
questions.justification: Routine and short.

questions.key_step: Determinant to a trigonometric equation, solve and filter by the interval.
questions.justification: Routine: determinant expansion, harmonic form, general solution; options also allow checking.

questions.key_step: Two linear parameter conditions via $D=0$ and $D_1=0$.
questions.justification: Routine; long arithmetic but a single idea.

questions.key_step: Row-reduce an augmented matrix and force the last row to vanish; then evaluate an expression.
questions.justification: Routine; simplest style of infinitely-many-solutions question.

questions.key_step: Spot that $R_2-2R_1$ (or $C_1-rC_2$) removes $r$, then expand.
questions.justification: The answer hinges on seeing the row operation; without it the direct expansion is lengthy and error-prone. One non-obvious but classic idea.

questions.key_step: Row operations (or rank-one lemma) then divide by $(\alpha-a)(\beta-b)(\gamma-c)$.
questions.justification: The decisive step is recognising the structure; algebra is short but easy to slip on signs and on $c$ versus $\gamma$.

questions.key_step: $|A|=0$ gives $\mu$, then the adjugate condition (or consistency) gives $\lambda$.
questions.justification: Two stages with a $3\times3$ adjugate; routine for a prepared student.

questions.key_step: Ugly coefficients hide the relation $R_3=9R_1+10R_2$; or reduce by row/column operations; two parameters.
questions.justification: Chain of several column/row operations with large numbers; precision risk, but the options help. Slightly above the routine two-parameter questions.

questions.key_step: Recognise a non-trivial solution as $D=0$ and expand, substituting $\alpha\beta\gamma=45$.
questions.justification: Short numerical question; one familiar criterion and a single expansion.

questions.key_step: Two linear conditions from $D_z=0$ and $D=0$.
questions.justification: Routine; two expansions.
